name: Siberian Russian
notes: Siberian old-settler Russian (сибирские старожильческие говоры: Novosibirsk, Tomsk, Krasnoyarsk). These are NORTHERN-based dialects — 'диалекты и говоры русского языка, развившиеся на основе севернорусского наречия' — so their vowel system is ОКАНЬЕ, not the 'partial аканье' this spec previously claimed while inheriting the standard's akanje table outright. ⟨о⟩ and ⟨а⟩ therefore stay [o] and [a] unstressed. Unlike the Northern zone proper, the old-settler dialects DISTINGUISH /ч/ and /ц/ ('различение «ч» и «ц», в то время как северорусским говорам свойственно цоканье'), so no цоканье is encoded and ⟨ч⟩ keeps the standard [tɕ]; and /г/ is the plosive [ɡ] ('взрывной [г]'), so this spec sits on the Northern side of the [ɣ] isogloss. The behaviour of unstressed vowels after SOFT consonants is deliberately left at the standard's иканье: the sources consulted state okanje for the hard context only, and extending it to a еканье system here would be a guess. NEEDS SOURCING. Genitive ⟨-ого/-его⟩ = [v] with okanje vowels ([-ovo], его = [jeˈvo]), for the same reason as `ru-x-northern`: the [v] desinence is morphological and crosses the okanje/akanje split. ENDING "ого" is the adjectival/pronominal genitive singular desinence ⟨-ого⟩ itself, realised [ovo]: ⟨г⟩ = [v], the ordinary Russian genitive desinence, which is morphological and so crosses the оканье/аканье isogloss unchanged, while the desinence VOWELS are okanje vowels — unstressed /o/ stays [o] and its counterpart after a soft consonant stays [e], so the ending is not the standard's reduced shape (Timberlake 2004; Comrie & Corbett 1993). location.notes: Novosibirsk — a representative city of the Siberian old-settler zone (with Tomsk and Krasnoyarsk). Siberia is 13 million km²: this point is close to meaningless as a summary and should be treated as such. [Wikidata Q883 P625]
